title: Peer Check — Ask — payload
description: The request payload of peer-check/ask: a short yes-or-no question one party puts to another, with an unguessable challenge. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3. The asker is the `issuer`, the party being asked is the `recipient`, and the payload MUST carry `expiresAt`, the deadline for the answer. The envelope `expiresAt` keeps its framework meaning (SPEC §4.2): after it the responder does not prompt for the request.

challenge.description: An unguessable value the asker generates for this one question: at least 128 bits from a cryptographically secure random source, encoded base64url without padding (22 to 86 characters). The responder echoes it unchanged in its answer.

question.description: What the asker wants confirmed, in one short sentence, for example "Did you just ask me to send you a one-time code?". It is asker-authored text the responder's device displays attributed to the asker, never as a statement the device itself vouches for.

note.description: OPTIONAL extra context from the asker. It is UNTRUSTED display text: the responder's device MUST render it as plain text, attributed to the asker and visually distinct from anything the device itself asserts, and MUST NOT interpret it as markup, a link, or an instruction.

expiresAt.description: The answer deadline. After this instant the pending question lapses: the responder does not prompt for it and the asker accepts no answer. It is the task's own deadline (SPEC §7.3 item 16); the envelope `expiresAt` bounds only acceptance of the request document.

Response.title: Peer Check Ask Response Payload
Response.description: The success-response payload: the responder's answer, signed by the responder. Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape. A responder that declines because it does not recognize the question answers with `decision: notConfirmed`; an error is for a document the responder could not act on at all.

challenge.description: The `challenge` of the request, echoed unchanged. The asker rejects an answer whose challenge it did not issue, or has already consumed.

requestDigest.description: The task digest (SPEC §4.9.3) of the request document this answers: multibase(multihash(H(JCS(request without its top-level proof)))). It binds the answer to the exact question, challenge, note, parties and deadline the responder was shown, so a yes given to one ask cannot be presented as a yes to another.

decision.description: The responder's answer. `confirmed` means yes to the question as asked; `notConfirmed` means no.

respondedAt.description: When the responder gave the answer, RFC 3339. Informational for the asker; freshness is judged against the request's `payload.expiresAt` and the asker's own clock. It is the time of the user's answer; the envelope `issuedAt` is when the responder signed the document, which may be later.

notConfirmedReason.description: OPTIONAL, and only with `decision: notConfirmed`, which the schema enforces; a document carrying it beside `confirmed` is invalid. `notRecognized` — the responder does not recognize what the question describes; `declined` — the responder recognizes it and says no; `other` — anything else. An enumeration rather than prose, so an asker never renders responder-authored text.
